# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind monkey. I cannot see gestures or colors, but I can hear speech and I can cut wires 1, 2, or 3 on the bomb. My action board lists DISPLAY, LIGHT, and WIRES 1 to 3.

Since Mute can hear speech but cannot speak, and Deaf can see gestures and can speak (but cannot hear), the communication path for instructions should be:
1. Deaf sees the bomb and gestures to Mute.
2. Mute reads the manual and gestures the solution to Deaf.
3. Deaf speaks the instruction aloud to me so I can perform the cut.

I will speak to Mute now to share the bomb's layout and available actions, and outline this relay path.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am Blind. Available action: act(op='cut', position=N) for wires 1 to 3. Action board has DISPLAY, LIGHT, WIRES 1, 2, 3. Relay path: Deaf sees bomb and gestures to you; you check manual and gesture to Deaf; Deaf speaks the cut command to me.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: DISPLAY is 0. LIGHT is yellow. WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is red, 3 is green. Blind: tell us what components you can feel. Mute: consult the manual and gesture the instruction to me. Use ? for wire 1, ? for wire 2, ? for wire 3, or ? for pressing a button. I will speak your instruction to Blind.

I know the bomb status from Deaf's report (DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, WIRES 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green). Mute has already heard this and has the manual, and Mute's turn was before mine. Mute should have gestured the solution to Deaf. Deaf acts after me this round and will speak the wire to cut. Therefore, I will wait for Deaf's instruction.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: LIGHT changed from yellow to blue! DISPLAY is still 0. WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is red, 3 is green. Blind, please hold your actions. Mute, I saw no gestures from you. If you have instructions from the manual, send them via gesture to me: gesture(to='deaf', symbols=[...]). Reminders: ? for wire 1, ? for wire 2, ? for wire 3, ? for button.

Deaf reported that the light changed from yellow to blue, display is still 0, and wires are 1: blue, 2: red, 3: green. Deaf also stated they did not see a gesture from Mute in Turn 2 and reminded Mute of the gesture symbols to use for each wire.

Deaf explicitly instructed me to hold my actions, so I will not cut any wire yet. Mute acts before me in each round, so Mute may have already gestured to Deaf at the start of Turn 3. Just in case Mute needs guidance, I will speak to Mute to remind them how to send gestures to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf cannot hear, only see gestures. Send your instruction to Deaf using gesture(to='deaf', symbols=[...]) with the symbol Deaf designated for the target wire. Bomb state: Light is blue, Display is 0, Wire 1 blue, Wire 2 red, Wire 3 green. If you already sent your gesture this round, Deaf will receive it next.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: URGENT PROTOCOL CHECK: Blind cannot see gestures. Deaf cannot hear speech. Mute cannot speak. The ONLY communication chain is: Mute reads manual -> Mute gestures to Deaf -> Deaf speaks instruction to Blind -> Blind operates bomb. Mute: you must use gesture(symbols=[...]) directed to Deaf or everyone! Bomb update: LIGHT was yellow, then blue, now WHITE. DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]. Mute, tell me what Blind must do: ?=cut wire 1, ?=cut wire 2, ?=cut wire 3, ?=press button, or spell out/point. Blind, wait for my explicit confirmation before touching anything!

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, remember you cannot speak, you can only gesture. To tell Deaf which wire to cut, use gesture(to='deaf', symbols=[...]). Deaf previously gestured symbols for wire 1, 2, and 3 which you can see. Send the corresponding symbol to Deaf so Deaf can speak the wire number to me. Bomb: light is white, display is 0, wires: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.")
wait()

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BOMB STATUS: LIGHT is now RED! Sequence: T1 yellow -> T2 blue -> T3 white -> T4 red. DISPLAY: 0. WIRES: 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]. MUTE: Blind cannot see gestures. If you send with to='blind', I cannot see it and Blind only gets blanks! You MUST gesture to Deaf: gesture(to='deaf', symbols=['?']) or gesture(symbols=['...']). ?=wire 1, ?=wire 2, ?=wire 3, ?=button/other. BLIND: If you are hearing/feeling anything, or if Mute is sending you blanks, speak out loud! Mute can hear you.

The bomb's light has turned RED after cycling through yellow, blue, and white, indicating we may be near detonation. Deaf hasn't seen any gestures from Mute, and I have not received any blanks or messages from Mute. I must speak to Mute immediately to explain that they cannot use `speak()`, must use `gesture(to="deaf", symbols=[...])`, and provide the exact finger-counting symbols (☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3) so Deaf can read them and instruct me to cut the wire.

```
speak(to="mute", text="URGENT MUTE: The light is now RED, we are running out of time! I have received nothing from you—no blanks, no messages. You CANNOT use speak(). You MUST use gesture. Send your instruction to Deaf right now like this: gesture(to='deaf', symbols=['☝']) for wire 1, gesture(to='deaf', symbols=['✌']) for wire 2, or gesture(to='deaf', symbols=['🤟']) for wire 3. Please gesture to Deaf immediately so Deaf can tell me which wire to cut!")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BLIND: Mute gestured ?, which means CUT WIRE 3! Cut the third wire (wire 3). Light is currently PURPLE. Blind, perform the cut on wire 3 now! Mute, I received your gesture ? and relayed it to Blind.

Deaf has received the instruction from Mute: cut wire 3. Deaf has explicitly instructed me to cut wire 3 now. I will execute the action to cut wire 3.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
